newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus war games show reservists ready, President.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus war games show reservists ready, President.

text.p: Cyprus's largest military exercises showed reservists were ready to fulfill their duties, President Glafcos Clerides said on Wednesday after the joint Greek and Greek Cypriot war games.

Eight-and-a-half thousand Greek Cypriot reservists took part in the Nikiforos exercise, held annually on the Mediterranean island, virtually partitioned since Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974.

"The reservists proved they are psychologically ready and determined to fulfill their duties," said the President, taking the salute from reservists who marched in the southern coastal town of Larnaca, signalling the end of the exercise.

Greek F-16 fighter jets made several appearances, hitting mock targets while a transport aircraft dropped Greek parachutists. Two fast attack craft, a destroyer, submarine and a frigate of the Greek navy also took part.
Two pairs of F-16 flew over Larnaca on Wednesday in formation during the reservists march. Two returned to base and the other two landed in Paphos, on the western coast of the island.
Turkey called on Greece and Cyprus not to repeat what it described as aggressive and provocative joint military exercises off the Turkish coast.

"We expect such exercises to end immediately. Otherwise precautions matching this kind of provocations and actions may be put on the agenda," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.
Greek Cypriot television stations transmitted extensive footage from the exercise, disrupting normal schedules to provide live links.
Clerides said Greece's participation was in accordance to a 1993 defence pact between the two countries.
Under terms of the pact, Greece is to come to Cyprus's aid in the event of further hostilities on the island with Turkey.
Turkish troops invaded the north five days after a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup in July 1974 inspired by the military regime ruling in Athens at the time.
Turkey has 30,000 troops stationed in northern Cyprus, where Turkish Cypriots have declared a breakaway state, recognised only by Ankara.
Greek and Turkish Cypriots live separately with a 180 km (112 miles) long United Nations-controlled buffer zone between them.
Defence Minister Costas Eliades told reporters the national guard was a 'deterrent force' on the island.
"Our aim is to achieve a peaceful solution to the Cyprus problem" said Eliades. "The National Guard will continue to upgrade until a solution is found."
